notes: Qemica can now drive ORCA as a second classical engine, using your own licensed install — the full range of calculation types, with the input file rendered in the app so you can read and edit it. Qemica does not include, download or host ORCA. The Run screen is now a table of every molecule in the project, sortable and filterable, with a lifecycle per molecule (empty, geometry prepared, ready to submit, in queue, running, complete, error) that survives a restart. An independent expert review of the ORCA integration fixed results that were wrong or empty: entropy was 298 times too large (the entropy term, an energy, stored in a per-kelvin field); thermochemistry ignored the temperature and pressure you set and silently used 298.15 K, which propagated into solvation, binding, pKa and redox free energies; triplet excited states were labelled singlets; the polarizability was computed but never read back; NMR anisotropy read zero for every nucleus; open-shell orbital ladders rendered empty; and molecular-dynamics and reaction-path axes carried frame indices where times and distances belonged. Recipes ORCA rejects are now refused while you compose them rather than after the queue, including a coupled-cluster case that failed while reporting success. Engine 0.1.5. Universal, signed and notarized macOS build. See the changelog: https://qemica-lab.com/changelog/
